correctness.rationale: The complete-graph Laplacian L(K_a)=a V_a with V_a=I-J_a/a and U_a=J_a/a. Tensor spectral projections U_a⊗U_b, V_a⊗U_b, U_a⊗V_b, V_a⊗V_b yield L eigenvalues 0,a,b,a+b and thus exactly four kernel equality classes. Three classes are strictly positive for every t>0; only vertices differing in both coordinates have entry F_ab/(ab), negative immediately since F_prime(0)=-2ab. Writing H(t)=exp(b^2 t)(1-exp(-a^2 t))/(1-exp(-(a^2+2ab)t)), its logarithmic derivative b^2+a^2/(exp(a^2t)-1)-(a^2+2ab)/(exp((a^2+2ab)t)-1) is positive because u/(exp(ut)-1) decreases with u. H(0+)=a/(a+2b)<1 and H(infty)=infty, so exactly one cutoff. Every row sums to one, with precisely (a-1)(b-1) potentially negative entries; its absolute row sum proves the norm formula. Multiplying F_prime by exp((a+b)^2t) gives a strictly increasing exponential equation with one positive root, giving a unique peak before cutoff. At a=b=m, factor 1-2z+z^4=(z-1)(z^3+z^2+z-1), derive tau=-log(z*)/m^2, theta=log2/(3m^2), max gain as stated. For fixed a and b large, y=b²t and delta=a/b expansions at the unique monotone zero and peak prove y_cut=log(2b/a)+O_a(log b/b), y_peak=1+O_a(1/b), max gain=4(a-1)/(eb)+O_a(b^-2). Independently computed five explicit small rook-graph matrix exponentials, entries, negativity and norm; infinite statements rely on analytic monotonicity and uniform expansions.

value.rationale: Fourth-order heat semigroups need not preserve positivity or maximum principles. Rook graphs are natural Cartesian products/line graphs with a complete four-level spectral decomposition. An exact worst-case maximum-coordinate norm and sharp eventual-positivity threshold for every rectangular parameter, including unusual logarithmic thin-board scaling, provide a motivated structural classification of transient positivity defects beyond general eventual-positivity existence criteria.

final_claim: For all integer a,b>=2, the unnormalized rook-graph squared-Laplacian heat exp(-tL^2) has exact infinity operator norm 1+2(a-1)(b-1)/(ab)[-F_ab(t)]_+, F_ab(t)=1-e^{-a^2t}-e^{-b^2t}+e^{-(a+b)^2t}. It is entrywise nonnegative exactly at t=0 and t>= a unique positive cutoff; its norm has one peak. Square-board constants are exact and fixed-a, b->infty cutoff grows logarithmically in b^2t while maximal amplification vanishes at rate 1/b.
limitations: Finite unweighted rectangular rook graphs with unnormalized Laplacian squared, t>=0, infinity norm; no conclusions for arbitrary weighted graphs, higher Cartesian factors or other fourth-order boundary models.
